newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albanian investors angry at pyramid scheme folding.
newsitem.headline: Albanian investors angry at pyramid scheme folding.

text.p: The manager of an Albanian pyramid savings scheme told thousands of angry investors on Wednesday in Tirana that their get-rich-quick plan had collapsed.
Hours earlier, part of the crowd had clashed with riot police during a protest called to demand their money back.
Maksude Kademi, a Romany gypsy woman who in November stopped repayments to depositors in one of the most high profile of the schemes, told the jeering crowd she had no money to give them.
"This was a pyramid scheme that failed. So you have no reason to (protest and) ask the state to give you money," Kademi, 30, said through a megaphone.

"I asked for a credit today but I could not get it. I will keep trying," she added, drawing boos and whistles from demonstrators, some of whom tried to break through a police cordon barring them from her western Tirana flat.

In the clash with police earlier, about 500 depositors broke away from a crowd of 5,000 near Kademi's home and scuffled with the officers blocking the route to Tirana's main Skanderbeg Square. Police made several arrests and eyewitnesses said some protesters were injured.

The opposition Socialists slammed President Sali Berisha and his conservative Democratic Party on Wednesday, accusing them of turning a blind eye to the pyramid schemes and plunging Albania into an economic crisis. They also called for mass protests.
Pyramid schemes, offering returns of up to 200 percent over three months, have sprung up across the impoverished Balkan state since the fall of communism in 1990.
The collapse of Kademi's scheme, known as "Sude's" from a diminuation of her given name, followed the demise of a similar scheme late last year. Four others have suspended repayments to investors.
"First they stole our votes and now they are trying to steal our money," one woman said, accusing the government of failing to keep its election promises of security and prosperity.
